The instant appeal is preferred against the  judgement and award dated 26 th June, 2019 passed  by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claim  Tribunal, A.D.J. Fast Track Court, Raiganj in MAC  Case No. 10 of 2015.

sentences.text: The brief fact of this case is that on 12.07.2007  at about 15.30 hrs the victim of this case namely  Hariram Agarwala was driving his car bearing  Registration No. WB-60B/3838 (Saantro Car) and  proceeding towards Raiganj side from Dalkhola side  through N.H. 34 along with his family members.

When the car reached near Nagor Bridge, at the time  one minor child was cycling over the National  Highway and suddenly trying to cross the road and  appeared just in front of the car, in order to save the  cyclist, the victim applied sudden break,
 unfortunately the car dashed the Toll Gate near  2 P.M.

sentences.text: The deceased Hari Ram Agarwala i.e. the driver cum owner of the vehicle succumbed to his injury after the accident.
The widow of the victim filed an application before the learned Tribunal for getting compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The claim case was contested by the Insurance Company by filing a written statement.

The learned Tribunal after hearing the parties and after receiving the evidences awarded a sum of Rs. 16,54,000/- as the compensation and directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation together with 6% interest per annum from the date of filing of the claim application.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said award the instant appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company.
Mr. Pahari, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Insurance company submits that the impugned award passed by the learned Tribunal is illegal and erroneous in the eye of law.
He submits that the facts suggest that owner cum driver of the vehicle died in the road traffic accident.
The victim is not the third party in true P.M.

2  3 sense, thus the claimants is not entitled to get any compensation according to the structure formula under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
 Mr. Pahari further submits that the Insurance policy suggest that the PA cover is Rs. 100 was paid to the Insurance company to cover the owner cum driver of the offending vehicle, which is a fixed amount of Rs. 2 lakhs.

sentences.text: He submits that claimant is entitled to get fixed compensetory amount of Rs. 2 lakhs in this case.

In support of his contention he cited two decisions, one of this court as well as Hon'ble Apex Court they are (i) Bajaj Allianz General Ins. Co. Ltd.
- Vs - Supriya Das & Anr. reported in 2011 ACJ 348 and (ii) National Insurance Company Limited - Vs - Ashalata Bhowmik & Ors. reported in 2018 ACJ 2825.

sentences.text: Heard the learned advocate and perused the LCR.
It appears that the policy certificate was marked as exhibit - 4 by the learned Tribunal.
In the liability portion the PA cover was Rs. 100/- and extra PA was 300/- at the end of such liability column

it was noted that "PA cover under Section III for owner- P.M. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Bimala Devi Agarwal on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143775487/
3 driver (CIS) Rs. 2 lakhs."
 4

In the case of Ashalata Bhowmik the Hon'ble Apex Court has held in paragraph 7 and 9 as follows : -
 "7.
We have carefully considered  the submissions of the learned  Counsel made at the Bar and perused  the materials placed on record.
It is  an admitted position that the  deceased was the owner-cum-driver of  the vehicle in question.
The accident  had occurred due to rash and  negligent driving of the vehicle by the  deceased.
No other vehicle was  involved in the accident.
The  deceased himself was responsible for  the accident.
The deceased being the  owner of the offending vehicle was not  a third party within the meaning of  the Act.
The deceased was the victim  of his own action of rash and  negligent driving.

A claimant, in our  view, cannot maintain a claim on the  basis of his own fault or negligence  and argue that even when he himself P.M. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Bimala Devi Agarwal on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143775487/
4  may have caused the accident on  5 account of his own rash and negligent driving, he can nevertheless make the insurance company to pay for the same.

entities.text: P.M. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Bimala Devi Agarwal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the respondents being the LRs of the deceased could not have maintained the claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
9. Therefore, the High Court was not justified in directing the appellant insurer to pay the compensation determined by the Tribunal.

Since the indemnification extended to personal accident of the deceased is limited to Rs. 2,00,000 under the contract of insurance, the respondents are entitled for the said amount towards compensation.

Hence, the appellant is directed to deposit the said sum of Rs. 2,00,000 with interest at the rate of 9 per cent per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal within a period of four weeks from today."

The law has been decided by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ashalata Bhowmik on the question that whether claimants can maintain a claim for death of owner/insurerd, the answer was negative, but it has been held that since vehicle was insured and premium was paid for personal accident (PA) cover of owner cum driver up to 2 lakhs, the insurance company is directed to pay Rs. 2 lakhs for personal accident cover of owner insured.

Considering the observation of the Hon'ble Apex Court of Ashalata Bhowmik and also considering the insurance policy (exhibit - 4) it appears to me that the deceased was the owner cum driver of the offending vehicle who died in the road traffic accident; the personal accident cover for owner cum driver is two lakhs.
So, in this case the claimant is entitled to get the fixed compensation of Rs. 2 lakhs.
The award passed by the learned Tribunal appears to be not justified.
Thus the award is hereby modified.
The claimant is entitled to get compensation accounting to Rs. 2 lakhs along with 6% interest per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till its actual payment.

It appears that at the time of filing of the instant appeal the Insurance Company has deposited the statutory amount of Rs. 25,000/- on 17.09.2019 and thereafter also deposited an amount of Rs.
23,70,195/- on 29.08.2022 thus the Insurance company has deposited in all an amount of Rs.
23,95,195/-.
P.M.

After such disbursement there may have residue in the account of the Insurance company, that may be refunded to the Insurance company along with the accrued interest on usual prayer.
The instant appeal FMA 874 of 2022 is disposed of.
Pending applications, if any are also disposed of.
All parties shall act on the server copy of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.

(Subhendu Samanta, J.)
